results.rule: Bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, subscript and superscript all survive.
Inline code containing a backtick or a pipe keeps those characters literally.
Text that looks like Markdown syntax is escaped so it renders as literal characters.
External links, mail links and in-page anchors are all preserved.
A link to another exported page points at that page, not into the wiki.
Emoji and non-Latin text survive unchanged.
A soft line break stays a line break inside one paragraph, not a paragraph split.
A quote nested inside a quote keeps its depth.
Heading levels 3 through 6 are preserved as distinct levels.
A code macro with a language produces a fence that declares that language.
Every declared language round-trips, not just the first one.
A code macro title is not silently dropped.
A fence written inside a code block does not terminate the block early.
A long line inside a code block is not wrapped.
Non-ASCII text inside a code block survives.
A noformat macro becomes a code block, keeping its whitespace.
A completed task exports as completed. Flipping a task to incomplete changes a fact.
A bullet list nested three levels deep keeps all three levels.
An ordered list nested inside an ordered list stays nested.
Two paragraphs in one list item stay two paragraphs, and are never concatenated.
A code block inside a list item stays inside that item and does not split the list.
A table inside a list item is not deleted. Markdown cannot nest it, so it must degrade visibly.
A quote inside a list item survives.
A table becomes a Markdown table, and inline marks inside cells survive.
Empty cells do not shift the remaining columns.
Merged cells cannot be expressed in Markdown, but their text must not be lost.
Block content inside a cell (a list, a code block, two paragraphs) is not dropped.
A line break inside a cell stays a line break.
A table whose cells hold CJK text still parses as a table.
Attached images are written out as files.
Image references in the body point at the exported files.
An attachment whose name contains a space is exported and correctly referenced.
An attachment with a non-ASCII filename is exported and still identifiable.
An image referenced by external URL is kept as an external reference.
An image wrapped in a link produces valid Markdown — a link containing an image.
An image inside a table cell stays inside the table.
A non-image attachment is exported and linked relatively, not back to a wiki URL.
Panel text survives. A panel with no Markdown equivalent must degrade, never delete.
Block content inside a panel survives too.
Collapsed content is still exported. Being hidden is not the same as being absent.
Status lozenge text survives.
Dates survive in a readable form.
Excerpt text survives.
An include macro does not abort the export.
An unknown third-party macro still yields its body text.
Column layouts flatten in reading order with no cell dropped.
A code block inside a layout cell survives with its language.
No exported filename is an opaque placeholder such as page-<uuid>.md.
A page titled only in Korean still produces a filename a human can identify.
A title mixing Korean with one ASCII word does not collapse to that word alone.
Two titles that differ only in discarded characters produce two distinct files.
A title containing punctuation illegal in filenames is exported safely, not dropped.
A title containing emoji is exported without crashing.
A bulk export reaches the whole subtree, including great-grandchildren.
The exported directory structure mirrors the page hierarchy.
Every page in the corpus appears exactly once in the export.
